races.display_title: Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (Group 3)
races.verdict: STARLUST was best of the home team in the Nunthorpe and confirmed himself as still in good form despite being positioned away from the other principals at the Curragh last week. He can capitalise on the drop in grade at the chief expense of Redorange , who looks well up to making his presence felt in minor Group company. Diligent Harry can complete the 1-2-3. STARLUST REDORANGE DILIGENT HARRY

races.display_title: Dubai Duty Free Autumn Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: FRENCH DUKE ran subsequent listed winner Plage de Havre to within a nose at the Ebor Festival last month and he can go one place better despite a 5 lb rise. Primo Lara was in the frame behind the selection at York and has since scored at Kempton, so merits plenty of respect, whilst Pearl River is also a player with the step back up in trip likely to suit. FRENCH DUKE (IRE) PRIMO LARA (IRE) PEARL RIVER

races.verdict: KICKING BEAR 'S debut was chock-full of promise and with the promise of plenty more to come, he should take some stopping. As you'd expect for an autumn Newbury maiden there's plenty of depth to this, with Kodiac City promising in his own right, while Iron Stone Lad and Coloniser are perhaps the pick of the newcomers. KICKING BEAR (FR) KODIAC CITY (IRE) IRON STONE LAD

races.verdict: Winner of 2 of his 3 starts last year, CASTLE ROCK ran to a useful level when second at Newmarket on handicap/seasonal debut in August and he can build on that effort to add to his tally. races.verdict: SILENT BEAUTY banished the memory of her Albany flop with an impressive listed success at Ripon 19 days ago and can make her mark at Group level now. races.verdict: A valuable novice in which the vote goes to newcomer GOLDEN SOUK , who ticks plenty of boxes on paper for a quality yard. races.verdict: HUMPHREY hasn't looked altogether straightforward when a beaten favourite on both of his starts, but his form is strong and the 7 lb he receives from debut-winner Amazonica may prove decisive. Sir Hannibal also brings solid novice form to the table but he's been off the track for over 13 months. HUMPHREY AMAZONICA (IRE) SIR HANNIBAL (GER)

races.display_title: Kidsbank Chester Handicap
races.verdict: KIRKDALE carried on where he'd left off earlier in the year when returning from 5 months off with an excellent second, and if he can transfer that progress back to turf then he could resume winning ways at the expense of Havana Rum , who is well treated now and will appreciate the return to 6f, while Supreme King could take a hand. KIRKDALE (IRE) HAVANA RUM (IRE) SUPREME KING (IRE)

races.verdict: The speed that SUDDEN FLIGHT showed last time suggests this drop back to 5f may suit. He'll be fine whatever the ground is and has a handy draw, so there are reasons to be hopeful. Over Spiced has been a model of consistency lately and is the second choice ahead of Copper Knight and the Paul Midgley pair Elegant Erin and Vingegaard . races.display_title: SIS, Supporting Irish Racing Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: HOPEFUL HERO confirmed he's in top form when runner-up at Kilbeggan 2 weeks ago and while he has a 3 lb rise to deal with, he may well be up to the job. Del Boys Diva shaped very well at that track herself last time, finding 19f too much of a test so she's second choice, with Littlefoot dangerous from this lower hurdles mark. HOPEFUL HERO (IRE) DEL BOYS DIVA (IRE) LITTLEFOOT (IRE)

races.display_title: BAR 1 Betting 'Best Odds Guaranteed Overnight' Flat Race
races.verdict: EL PARAISO makes plenty of appeal on paper for a yard going well with its bumper horses (last 3 all successful), so he gets the nod to continue that good run before market clues. Ellen Imlach is another appealing newcomer who warrants close scrutiny in the betting, while the form of Rocky Alfonso 's debut has worked out reasonably well and he's the narrow pick of those with experience, ahead of Walkwithmyfriend , who is turned out relatively quickly following a demanding race at Kilbeggan. EL PARAISO ELLEN IMLACH (FR) ROCKY ALFONSO (IRE)
